issues.legal_issue: A plaint cannot be rejected at the threshold for being barred by law when that bar depends on disputed facts or material beyond the plaint.
material_facts: An earlier partition suit resulted in a preliminary decree defining the parties’ shares, but the final-decree proceedings were dismissed without a partition of the land by metes and bounds.

The present suit sought partition of properties described in the earlier suit, and the parties disputed whether the properties had been divided, were available for partition, or had been separately possessed or alienated.
The trial court rejected the plaint, and the High Court affirmed, relying on the earlier proceedings and the asserted bar arising from them.
The Supreme Court found that determining the effect of the earlier proceedings and the availability and identity of the properties required factual adjudication beyond the plaint.
issues.conclusion: The plaint could not be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) on the basis of the disputed matters; the appeal was allowed and the parties were left free to raise their contentions at the appropriate stage.
issues.legal_principle: Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure applies where the suit appears from the statements in the plaint itself to be barred by law. For that inquiry, the plaint’s averments must be taken as true, without adding to or subtracting from them, and the court cannot consider evidence, the defence, or disputed questions of fact. Whether res judicata applies when it requires factual inquiry may be considered as a preliminary issue or at the final hearing, rather than under this rule. The Court relied on Liverpool & London S.P. & I Association Ltd. v. M.V. Sea Success I, C. Natrajan v. Ashim Bai, Popat and Kotecha Property v. State Bank of India Staff Association, Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust, and T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal; it also referred to Order XIV Rule 2 and to the earlier court’s invocation of Section 12 read with Order II Rule 2.

predicates.threshold_plaint_rejection_application: A party seeks rejection of a plaint at the threshold on the ground that the suit is barred by law.
predicates.bar_not_apparent_from_plaint: The alleged legal bar does not follow from the plaint’s statements when those statements are taken as true.
predicates.deciding_bar_requires_disputed_facts: Determining whether the legal bar applies requires resolving disputed facts or considering material beyond the plaint.

issues.definition: When a threshold application claims that a suit is barred by law, rejection at that stage is improper if the bar is not apparent from the plaint or deciding it requires resolving disputed facts.
